findings.reason: whichever section lands second, §12's test fails on `main` and §3's write paths grant nobody the right to repair it, so §12 must wait on §3 and gate only the recorded waiver, or §3 must grant the §12 test.
findings.text: §12's done-when asserts that `allow_unreconciled_runs` "behaves likewise for a session with an overdue run", meaning the entry queues with the waiver and is refused without it, but §3's deliverable makes a direct dispatch and a queue-time check succeed for exactly that session with `--allow-unreconciled-runs` changing nothing, so after §3 lands the refusal §12's gate depends on no longer exists

findings.reason: a coordinator taking the plan's own chain closes the followup having built §2–§9 and leaves §10–§14 unbuilt, and the body misstates which sections §9 waits on.
findings.text: the driving followup f-wftl-001 still reads "Build §2 to §9" and "§9 waits on §2 to §5", while `plan-section-declarations` now carries s10–s14 as implementable and `plan-section-depends-on` gives s9 the waits s2, s3, s4, s5 and s6

findings.reason: the roadmap is how a coordinator learns which sections of a plan are held, and a passing node could leave it reading the plan as wholly held or wholly ready.
findings.text: §10's deliverable requires that plan readers, the roadmap and the plan schema report the sections a decision names, but its done-when asserts only dispatch and admission behaviour, so a node that scopes the hold correctly and exposes the named sections nowhere still passes

findings.reason: the verdict row is the surface §1's own evidence is drawn from, so a node can pass while that row still omits the decision key.
findings.text: §11's deliverable names three surfaces that must carry the blocker (the dispatch result, the queued pointer's recorded hold, the admission verdict) but its done-when asserts only the first two, so the admission verdict a coordinator reads in `admission-verdicts.jsonl` can go unchanged

findings.reason: the node must either implement an unstated ordering guard or fail its own gate, so the deliverable should state the refusal or the control should become a mutation that drops the prediction write.
findings.text: §8's negative control is "a prediction recorded after the review was stored is refused by the view", a refusal no part of its deliverable states: the deliverable asks only that the prediction is recorded before dispatch and the outcome recorded beside it when the review is stored, and a view that reports the recorded rows satisfies every stated requirement and fails the control
